title: Vybe vs Viktor: Which AI Agent Platform Fits Your Team in 2026?
summary: Vybe vs Viktor in 2026: both run real work across your tools, but they split on durable apps, per-agent isolation, and security. See which AI agent platform fits your team.
body_text: Your team does not need another tool. You need something that runs the tools you already have. That is the promise behind both Vybe and Viktor: AI that does real work instead of just answering questions. But the two platforms get there in very different ways, and the gap is wider than the marketing suggests. Viktor brands itself as "Not a tool. A hire." It drops one AI employee into your Slack and Teams, and everyone on the team talks to it. Vybe gives you a team of specialized agents, each with its own role, memory, tools, and the apps they build and operate themselves. Here is how they actually compare, and the three structural differences that decide which one fits your team. What each platform actually does Vybe Vybe is a platform where AI agents build apps, connect to your tools, and run workflows autonomously. You create agents the way you would staff an org chart: give each one a name, a job description, and access to the systems it needs. An agent named Aaron runs product research. Another named Derrick runs the blog. A third owns customer success. Each agent works where your team already does (Slack, email, meetings, WhatsApp), connects to 3,000+ integrations plus a real browser, and builds its own internal apps when the job calls for one. Agents get sharper over time through a persistent memory of notes and skills. Vybe is backed by a $10M seed round led by First Round Capital and runs in production with enterprise design partners, including companies with 300 to 400+ employees. Viktor Viktor is a single AI coworker that now lives in both Slack and Microsoft Teams. You install it once, and everyone messages it like a colleague. It connects to 3,200+ tools through managed connectors and OAuth, pulls data, runs analysis, reviews code and pull requests, and returns outputs like PDFs, spreadsheets, dashboards, and deployed web apps. Viktor advertises SOC 2 compliance and a free tier of $100 in credits. On the surface the two look similar: connect your stack, talk in chat, get work back. The real differences show up in three places. Durable apps you own vs output that scrolls away This is the deepest difference between the two. Viktor runs a task and posts the result back into the chat thread: a PDF, a spreadsheet, an app link. The work is done, but the thing that produced it does not stick around. Next week, when you need the same recap, you re-prompt and it runs again. The output lives in your Slack history. Vybe agents build, deploy, and operate durable applications inside their own sandboxes. The app is not a deliverable you have to babysit. It is permanent operational software your team logs into. A concrete example from our own stack: Vybe's competitive-tracking agent, Competitor Radar, built and maintains a live database app that refreshes competitor intelligence on a schedule. Nobody re-prompts it. It runs, stores, and updates on its own. A sales agent builds a pipeline tracker wired to HubSpot and refreshes it every 30 minutes. A finance agent builds an AR dashboard and flags anomalies before anyone asks. Viktor can build a web app on request. Vybe agents build apps as part of the job, then keep operating them. You can see examples of agent-built internal tools in the Vybe gallery . The short version: Viktor drops files in chat. Vybe builds the operational software your team owns and logs into. Per-agent isolation vs one workspace-level identity Both platforms connect to thousands of tools. The question enterprise buyers actually ask is what each AI can see. Viktor is one identity installed at the workspace level. It inherits your Slack and Teams SSO, authenticates per-user OAuth, and reads across the connected surface. There is one Viktor, so there is no way to scope what one role sees versus another. It is ambient access by design. Vybe scopes access per agent. Your HR agent connects to Lucca and Google Calendar. Your sales agent connects to HubSpot and Gmail. Each agent runs in its own permissioned sandbox and only touches what it is explicitly granted. Your HR agent never sees sales data unless you configure it to. Both platforms are now SOC 2 compliant, so the compliance badge is not the dividing line. Architecture is. A workspace-wide AI with ambient read access is a different risk posture than a set of isolated agents, each scoped to one domain. For a CIO weighing what an AI can reach across the company, per-agent isolation is the more defensible answer. Vybe also supports SSO via Google Workspace and RBAC with per-agent permission controls today. A team of specialists vs a single generalist Viktor gives you one AI. Everyone talks to the same Viktor. That is simple to set up and easy to understand, and for a small team where one person covers ops, marketing, and finance, a single capable generalist is often enough. Vybe gives you a team, each agent purpose-built for a role. Your chief of staff agent does not share context with your sales agent. Your compliance agent has different permissions than your content agent. Each one accumulates domain-specific memory and develops the depth of a specialist instead of staying a generalist that knows a little about everything. Real work is specialized. The agent managing your CRM pipeline should not share a system prompt, tool access, or learned habits with the one writing your blog. Separation of concerns applies to AI workers the same way it applies to teams. Under the hood, Vybe also routes work across model providers like Gemini, GPT, and Claude based on cost and performance, so you are not tied to any single vendor's pricing or roadmap. Feature comparison at a glance App building: Viktor builds web apps on request. Vybe agents build apps and then operate them autonomously on a schedule. Automation: Viktor's heartbeat suggests workspace-wide automations you approve. Vybe agents run their own cron jobs, each scoped to its domain, so your blog agent's workflows never collide with your sales agent's. Integrations: roughly a draw on count, 3,000+ for Vybe and 3,200+ for Viktor, both over OAuth, both with browser access. The difference is per-agent scoping versus workspace-level access. Channels: Viktor lives in Slack and Teams. Vybe agents work across Slack, email, meetings, WhatsApp, and SMS. Security: both are SOC 2 compliant. Vybe adds per-agent RBAC, scoped permissions, and data isolation today. Pricing Viktor: Free tier: $100 in credits, no credit card required Paid plans start at $50/month Enterprise: custom pricing Vybe: Free tier available Team and Enterprise plans with custom pricing See vybe.build/pricing for current details Viktor's credit model is transparent but can be hard to predict once you lean on heavy automation. Vybe's pricing scales with the agents and usage you put into production. Who should choose which Viktor is a good fit if: You are a small team that wants one AI assistant in Slack or Teams Your work is mostly ad-hoc: pull a report, draft an email, answer a question You want the simplest possible setup You do not need per-agent isolation or scoped RBAC Vybe is the better fit if: You want specialized agents, each with a distinct role, memory, and toolset You need agents that build and operate their own apps, not just generate them once Security requires per-agent RBAC, scoped permissions, and data isolation You are running production workflows across multiple departments You want AI workers that learn and get sharper over time FAQ Is Viktor an AI agent platform or an AI assistant? Viktor positions itself as a single AI employee that works across your tools from inside Slack and Teams. Vybe is a platform for creating multiple specialized agents, each an autonomous worker with its own apps, tools, and memory. What is the real difference between Vybe and Viktor? Viktor returns work as messages and files in chat. Vybe agents build durable apps they keep operating, and each agent is isolated with its own scoped access instead of one workspace-wide identity. Are both platforms SOC 2 compliant? Yes. Both Vybe and Viktor advertise SOC 2 compliance. Vybe adds per-agent data isolation and RBAC, so access is scoped to each agent rather than granted at the workspace level. Do both platforms work with Slack and Teams? Yes. Viktor is native to Slack and Microsoft Teams. Vybe agents work across Slack, email, meetings, WhatsApp, and SMS. Try Vybe today If you want AI agents that do not just chat but build, connect, and run your workflows autonomously, start with Vybe for free .

The single-use ophthalmic program is Precision Optics’ second single-use program to move into production, further highlighting the Company’s growth opportunity in single-use endoscopy. title: Compare Leading AI Note-Automation Platforms for Vet Clinics
summary: A side-by-side comparison of veterinary AI note-automation platforms — what to evaluate, where competitors fall short, and how to calculate true ROI.
body_text: In May 2026, the daily reality for many veterinary professionals is a battle against an avalanche of administrative work. Industry data reveals that veterinarians can spend up to 40% of their day on administrative tasks [1] , while client communications suffer, with an average of 24% of inbound calls going unaddressed [2] . This administrative burden is a primary driver of burnout and erodes valuable time that could be spent on patient care. AI note-automation platforms have emerged as a powerful solution, but choosing the right one is critical. The best AI tools for automating clinical notes in veterinary practice do far more than just transcribe dictation; they function as a true copilot, streamlining your entire clinical workflow. This guide compares the leading platforms to help you find a solution that gives you back your time and lets you focus on what truly matters: the pets. Why Your Practice Needs More Than Just a Transcription Service A basic transcription service turns speech into text, but it often leaves you with a raw block of words that still needs to be structured, edited, and manually entered into your Practice Management System (PIMS). This only solves a fraction of the documentation problem. The risk is paying for a tool that creates a new bottleneck, leaving your team to do the heavy lifting of formatting, correcting terminology, and performing manual data entry. A comprehensive AI platform, by contrast, automates the entire documentation lifecycle. It actively listens to a consultation and then generates structured notes, creates client-friendly summaries, identifies billable items, and even assists with diagnostic reasoning. The goal isn't just to type for you; it's to think with you, freeing up hours in your day [3] . Key Features to Evaluate in a Veterinary AI Platform When comparing AI platforms, it's essential to look beyond marketing claims and evaluate the features that deliver tangible value. Here is a clear framework for assessing your options. Core Documentation Automation The cornerstone of any great platform is its ability to intelligently automate documentation. While a basic tool might offer dictation, a top-tier solution uses a single recorded consultation to automatically generate a suite of documents within seconds [4] : Structured SOAP Notes: Automatically formatted Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan notes ready for review. Exam Findings and Treatment Plans: Detailed and consistent records of the clinical encounter. Professional Discharge Summaries: Plain-language summaries for pet owners to improve compliance and understanding [5] . Billable Items: A list of charges captured from the conversation, improving cashflow and preventing missed revenue [5] . Clinical Intelligence & Diagnostic Support A true AI copilot acts as an extension of your clinical team. The most advanced platforms offer built-in diagnostic support connected to trusted, evidence-based sources. For instance, Vetnio's VetsGPT is a science-based reasoning assistant that helps clinicians summarize patient history, interpret lab and blood test results, and guides examinations with literature-backed insights, augmenting your professional judgment rather than replacing it [6] . PIMS Integration and Workflow Compatibility An AI tool should simplify your life, not complicate it with another data silo. Seamless integration with your existing PIMS is non-negotiable. The risk of choosing a non-integrated tool is creating workflow friction and data fragmentation. Top-tier platforms enhance the tools you already use, allowing you to generate and import notes without constantly switching applications. Vetnio, for example, integrates directly with leading systems like Provet Cloud — used by over 55,000 professionals — as well as Sonetas Fuga and Animana, fitting directly into your established workflow [7] . Mobile Accessibility & Ease of Use Veterinary medicine doesn't just happen in the exam room. You need a tool that moves with you. A dedicated mobile app with an offline-first recording design is crucial for fieldwork, ensuring you can capture data anywhere and sync it later [4] . Features like built-in calling and collaborative team workspaces ensure your staff stay connected and consistent, all without requiring expensive new hardware. The platform should be intuitive and easy to get started with minimal training. Security and Compliance When dealing with sensitive patient and client data, security and compliance are paramount. A data breach carries not just financial penalties but also a severe loss of client trust. Ensure any platform you consider is GDPR-compliant , uses enterprise-grade encryption, and undergoes regular, independent penetration testing to protect your practice and your clients [8] . Head-to-Head: Vetnio vs. The Competition The veterinary AI market is growing rapidly, with a projected global value set to exceed $2.6 billion by 2033 [9] . While many new players are emerging, their capabilities vary significantly. Vetnio: The Complete Clinical Copilot Vetnio stands apart as an all-in-one platform built to address the entire clinical workflow. Its strength lies in its three natively integrated pillars: AI Scribe: Fully automates the generation of clinical notes, client emails, and billable items. Crucially, the AI learns each veterinarian's individual tone and phrasing over time, ensuring notes are not only fast but also personalized and accurate [8] . This proven approach saves an average of 15 minutes per consultation . VetsGPT: Provides science-based diagnostic support, helping you reason through complex cases with insights backed by trusted literature [8] . Vetnio Assistants: Handles client communications, including appointment bookings and updates via channels like WhatsApp, ensuring your clinic stays connected and responsive [10] . With zero customer churn since its launch, Vetnio has proven its value in practices across the UK, Europe, and the USA [5] . Competitor Analysis: ScribbleVet, CoVet, and VetRec Platforms like ScribbleVet, CoVet, and VetRec are notable competitors and represent some of the best AI tools for automating clinical notes in veterinary practice [11] . ScribbleVet & CoVet: Both are capable AI scribes that generate SOAP notes from recordings and offer PIMS integrations. However, they differ in focus. CoVet is designed for team-based, multi-location practices needing structured workflows, while ScribbleVet is geared more toward individual clinicians [12] . The risk lies in their narrower scope. While they are expanding capabilities through partnerships — such as ScribbleVet's with radiology tool Vetology [9] — this can lead to a disjointed user experience compared to a natively unified platform. VetRec & VetNotes: These platforms are often characterized as powerful dictation-to-transcription services [13] . They excel at converting voice to text, but the risk is that they stop there. This requires more manual effort from your team to structure that text into complete, compliant SOAP notes, client summaries, and billable items, diminishing the overall time savings. Other players like Artiprax [14] and HappyDoc [15] also focus heavily on the note-generation aspect. Niche Players: Vetology, VetGPT.com, and GekkoVet To understand the full landscape, it's worth noting specialized tools. Vetology offers AI-assisted radiology reports [16] , while GekkoVet serves as an online diagnostic reference guide [13] . Other platforms like VetGPT.com [17] and Vetz.ai [18] also offer specific workflow automations. While valuable in their own right, the risk of relying on multiple niche tools is increased cost, complexity, and the same workflow fragmentation you are trying to avoid. They solve specific problems rather than serving as a comprehensive copilot for the entire clinical process. Making the Right Choice for Your Clinic Choosing the right platform is a strategic decision that will impact your team's daily happiness and your practice's bottom line. Here's how to make an implementation-focused choice. Step 1: Assess Your True Bottlenecks Look beyond the initial pain point of note-taking. For one week, have your team track time spent on specific administrative tasks: writing SOAP notes, drafting client follow-up emails, handling phone calls, and researching complex cases. The data will reveal where your biggest time sinks are and whether a simple scribe is enough, or if you need a comprehensive platform like Vetnio that addresses documentation, communication, and diagnostics. Step 2: Insist on a Live Integration Demo Don't compromise on integration. A tool that forces your team to constantly switch between apps or manually transfer data is counterproductive. Ask vendors for a live demo showing the integration with your specific PIMS . A pre-recorded video is not enough. If they cannot demonstrate a seamless workflow with your existing software, that is a major red flag about their real-world usability [19] . Step 3: Calculate the ROI Beyond the Subscription Fee The true return on investment isn't just about the monthly fee. Calculate your potential savings with a simple formula: (Time saved per vet, per day) x (Average hourly vet rate) = Daily cost savings Then, factor in the value of improved charge capture, reduced burnout risk, faster onboarding for new staff, and better patient outcomes. Saving 15 minutes per consultation allows you to be more present with each client, see more patients without feeling rushed, and dramatically reduce burnout [20] . Conclusion: The Future of Veterinary Documentation is Integrated and Intelligent While many AI scribes can take dictation, the real transformation comes from a platform that is deeply integrated, clinically intelligent, and automates work across your entire practice. By offloading documentation, streamlining client communications , and providing diagnostic support, a true AI copilot empowers you to focus on the reason you became a veterinarian in the first place: to provide the best possible care for animals. For practices ready to reclaim their time and embrace the future of veterinary medicine, Vetnio offers the most comprehensive, secure, and integrated solution on the market, validated by real-world news and partnerships .
